bullets.text: Halvern Dam on the Sorrel River above Brindlemark in the Assek Valley was reported damaged on 9 September 2025, with the right abutment affected.
Damage to the dam and its right abutment raised the risk of failure, and the alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange the following morning.
No casualties were reported in the window; roughly 11,800 residents were moved out of Brindlemark and people were evacuated from Ferris Hollow.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provided information on the dam, and a mandatory evacuation of Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow was under way at the end of the window.
Halvern Dam and the right abutment are reported damaged on the afternoon of the first day.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provides information on the dam damage.
The next morning a mandatory evacuation is ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow; the alert level is raised from Yellow to Orange.
Roughly 11,800 residents are moved out of Brindlemark and people are evacuated from Ferris Hollow.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment were damaged.
A mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow after the dam damage was confirmed.
Roughly 11,800 residents were evacuated from Brindlemark, with further residents moved out of Ferris Hollow.
The primary hazard was the potential failure of Halvern Dam following damage to the structure and its right abutment.
Authorities moved residents out of Brindlemark under the mandatory evacuation order within the first day of the dam damage report.
The alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange as the mandatory evacuation of Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow was ordered.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provided information on the condition of Halvern Dam after the damage was reported.
